title: Exact constant-coefficient module sheafification on sieve sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows with common target closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves are stable under pullback of sieves and satisfy transitivity. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ or subcanonicity are assumed. Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $\underline\Lambda$ be the associated sheaf of rings of the constant presheaf, and let $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$. A module sheaf over $\underline\Lambda$ is a sheaf of abelian groups with compatible $\underline\Lambda(T)$-actions on sections; morphisms respect these actions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\mathcal A$ for their abelian category and $i:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P$ for restriction of scalars along $\Lambda\to\underline\Lambda(T)$. There is an exact left adjoint $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$ to $i$. Its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of the underlying presheaf, and its unit is the usual sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The counit $bi\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ is an isomorphism, and $i$ is fully faithful. The essential image of $i$ consists exactly of those $\Lambda$-module presheaves whose underlying abelian presheaf is a sheaf. Thus a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules has a unique compatible $\underline\Lambda$-module structure.
